import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
class FFN(nn.Module):
def __init__(self):
super().__init__()
self.fc1 = nn.Linear(28 * 28, 256)
self.fc2 = nn.Linear(256, 10)
def forward(self, x):
x = F.relu(self.fc1(x))
logits = self.fc2(x)
return logits
X = torch.rand(64, 28 * 28) # a batch of 64 images
logits = FFN()(X)
print(logits.shape)
print(F.softmax(logits, dim=1).shape)
Output

Tokenization · Text Input07

Representing Text Input

Token: one piece of text represented by an entry in a model's vocabulary.

Vocabulary: the fixed collection of token pieces a tokenizer can represent.

Tokenization · Text Input08

Tokenization

Tokenization: the procedure that splits text into pieces and maps those pieces to token IDs. Token ID: an integer label assigned to a vocabulary entry.

Tokenizer's Vocabulary

TokenToken ID
"."0
"The"1
" and"2
" ate"3
" cat"4
" mat"5
" on"6
" sat"7
" the"8

Encoding: converting text into token IDs.

Tokenization · Text Input09

Decoding

Decoding: reconstructing text from token IDs.

TokenToken ID
"."0
"The"1
" and"2
" ate"3
" cat"4
" mat"5
" on"6

" the"8

The token IDs capture no intrinsic meaning.

Comparing IDs does not measure meaning.

Tokenization · Tokenization Levels14

Subwords in the Brain

Rastle, Davis and New (Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 2004): a word flashed too quickly to notice makes people faster at reading a second word, when the first looks like it's built from the second.

flashedthen readrelated byfaster by
cleanerCLEANmeaning and pieces27 ms
cornerCORNpieces only (corn + er)22 ms
brothelBROTHletters only ("el" isn't an ending)4 ms

Readers split words into pieces by  , not meaning. irishQwen's tokenizer does too:

  • ·cleaner → ·c le an er, ·corner → ·c or n er
  • ·brothel → ·b r ot he l (no oth, unlike ·broth → ·b r oth)

Different pieces though: readers know real endings like "-er", BPE only knows what was common in Shakespeare.
